case_title: SUKUMARAN v. STATE REP. BY THE INSPECTOR OF POLICE
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w ss.109 and 203; Tamil Nadu Forest Act s.36-A and E; Arms Act s.3 r/w s.25(1-B)(a)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302, s.203 IPC, s.36-A and E of Tamil Nadu Forest Act, s.3 r/w s.25(1-B)(a) of Arms Act
high_court_outcome: Partially allowed appeal, altered conviction under s.302 to s.304 Part II, acquitted from other charges
neutral_facts: The accused, a forest ranger, was on duty in his official jeep with his driver when he noticed four individuals in a lorry suspected of smuggling sandalwood. He chased the lorry, and after the driver and his associates started pelting stones at him and shouting 'fire them', the accused fired a shot from his DBL-gun, killing the driver. The accused then retrieved sandalwood and a gun from the lorry, and with the help of his driver, apprehended two of the deceased's associates. The accused lodged a complaint stating he fired in self-defense. The prosecution alleged murder, but the trial court convicted the accused under various sections. The High Court partially acquitted the accused, and the Supreme Court ultimately acquitted him, finding the prosecution failed to prove the incident's manner and the accused had a reasonable apprehension of harm.
